issue_context.title: SerialStream doesn't override memory-based Read-/WriteAsync methods
issue_context.body:
When adding a `NetCoreAppCurrent` configuration to System.IO.Ports, roslyn warns that SerialStream's memory-based `ReadAsync` and `WriteAsync` methods aren't overridden. I was unsure if this requires api-approval so I'm filing this issue.

```
/home/vihofer/runtime/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System/IO/Ports/SerialStream.cs(13,35): error CA1844: 'SerialStream' overrides array-based 'ReadAsync' but does not override memory-based 'ReadAsync'. Consider overriding memory-based 'ReadAsync' to improve performance. [/home/vihofer/runtime/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System.IO.Ports.csproj]
/home/vihofer/runtime/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System/IO/Ports/SerialStream.cs(13,35): error CA1844: 'SerialStream' overrides array-based 'WriteAsync' but does not override memory-based 'WriteAsync'. Consider overriding memory-based 'WriteAsync' to improve performance. [/home/vihofer/runtime/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System.IO.Ports.csproj]
```

cc @adamsitnik @carlossanlop @Jozkee @jeffhandley

@adamsitnik Should I take this to mean there's an interest in implementing the `ReadAsync` & `WriteAsync`  overloads (memory and array based) for the Windows version of `SerialStream` as well?

I've reconsidered that and most probably we should not do that for Windows as of now. The main reason is that testing this particular library is really hard and it would be easy to introduce a bug to the product. I am going to close both issues. @i3arnon thanks!

review_comments:
Not really. They get passed to a shared `DoIORequest`:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/851f09c96aaef293b802eb98fd06948c7719f6a3/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System/IO/Ports/SerialStream.Unix.cs#L806-L826

And used with the same type of delegate:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/851f09c96aaef293b802eb98fd06948c7719f6a3/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System/IO/Ports/SerialStream.Unix.cs#L731-L734

we had similar issue in `FileStream` and we were able to always store `ReadOnlyMemory` and cast it to `Memory` using `MemoryMarshal.AsMemory`

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6fc8441311120c47c96b2605bf3a0d186f82454a/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/Microsoft/Win32/SafeHandles/SafeFileHandle.ThreadPoolValueTaskSource.cs#L98

Since this project targets .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET 4.6.1:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6fc8441311120c47c96b2605bf3a0d186f82454a/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System.IO.Ports.csproj#L7

We can't do it here as this method is not available for these TFMs:

https://apisof.net/catalog/61409471-3239-9645-a842-a812d650f79f

> Since this project targets .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET 4.6.1:

Is that why some of the builds break? The memory overloads for Stream don't exist in 4.6.1. Should they be ifdef-ed?

What about the Windows part? I know it's very archaic, but it seems that the implementation uses `ReadFile` and `WriteFile` methods, which means that we could just create a `FileStream`  (with buffering disabled by passing `bufferSize: 1`) from the `SafeFileHandle` we get in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6fc8441311120c47c96b2605bf3a0d186f82454a/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System/IO/Ports/SerialStream.Win32.cs#L11-L13 and delegate all reads and writes to `FileStream`.
I'll take a look, but it feels like a separate PR to me..
